_doc: The valley town's people (#756, No Law step 1; docs/missions/BUILD_ORDER.md 0.3): who's in town when, where they stand or sit, and the few props they need, read by ValleyFolk (src/people/valley_folk.gd). A point is `lot` + `at` [a, b]: a metres east of the lot's west side (its x0), b metres back from the street front (north lots: -z, south lots: +z); y the ground's (plus `up`). Each townsman's `day` (townsfolk step 2, #870; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §3): blocks by the hour, each `from` an hour to the next block's (the last runs round to the first), `at` a named spot (`spots`) or `in` a place (on the book: indoors, asleep, out of town), `do` what he does there; a `home` (where he's built and goes when nothing says otherwise). A new person is one entry here. With the clock running into a block (within `walk_in_h`) he walks there by the town's ways (ValleyTown.add_ways plus this file's `places`): out of the last block's door, along, in at the next one's; the clock set past it (a jump, a load at night) and he's there already. Nobody comes out of a door or goes in at one while you can see it (the book's `seen_m`). Sean's B on #755 (unanswered: B by default): the saloon stays a grey block, so the bar, the card table and the drinking are in the saloon's yard (saloon_annex, Sean #700) for now; when the spec saloon goes onto its lot (A, or #695's week) the set moves inside and the people with it.
status: PROPOSED (#756): who and where are this session's stand-ins; No Law's card (docs/missions/no-law.md) names the barman, the card player and Cody.

set._doc: The saloon yard's stand-in bar and card table. `bar`: the kit bar's middle, running along the yard (b) with its customers' side east (+x, `yaw` 90); `table`: the card table's middle, `chairs` its four chairs by compass round it (each facing the table); `lamps` lit oil lamps (OilLamp, lit 17-4) on the bar's and the table's tops.

piano._doc: The band's piano (#799, config/band.json): the kit's upright, its back to the saloon's east wall (yaw 90: its keys to +x, the yard), a kit chair `chair_out` before its middle for the pianist (props chair_piano).

stage_piano._doc: #938 (Sean on #938): Payday Night's second upright on saloon B's stage (the kit's upright_piano; the dance hall keeps its own, nobody hauls one up): in the building's space, its back to the stage's back partition at the west end, its keys to the curtain (yaw 180 in its space), clear of the wing's steps; the pianist's chair before it (props stage_piano, chair_stage_piano).

places._doc: The set's own places, added to the town's ways for the folk: each [a, b] in the set's lot (or in `lot`'s) and what it links to (another of these, or the nearest of the town's places with `nearest`).

saloonb_yard_back._doc: #938: up saloon B's outside stair to the upper hall, through the wing onto the stage (Payday Night's band; the walk saloon B's test walks). `hall` + `local` [x, y, z] in the building's space (y under 0.05: the ground there); `stair_to` a link up a stair. Round the stair's foot by the yard's back.

saloonb_stage._doc: up the wing's three steps (their ramp); along the stage clear of its upright's chair

livery._doc: The livery's door (townsfolk step 3): its lot has no walk, so no door place of its own (ValleyTown); on the dirt before its barn doors.

spots._doc: Named spots (townsfolk brief §3 "Spots"): where a man stands or sits and what he faces, belonging to the place, not the man, so anyone sent there fits. A spot is one of: `behind` a bar (`along` it, + north), `at_bar` (its customers' side), `chair` (the set's card table's, by compass: sat in it by a SitChore), or `lot` + `at` [a, b] (lot_point's) facing `faces` [a, b] (else the street). A day's block names one with `at` (or gives one inline) and says with `do` what he does there (SpotChore, townsfolk step 4, #957): stand, lean, sit, counter, sweep, carry, talk, drink, work, each a loop with its breaks; a spot may give `seat` (a kit prop stood there for `sit`), `tool` (`rug` for sweep: shaken, not swept; `anvil`, `bench` for work), `to` [a, b] (where carry takes the pile), `reach` (how far along sweep goes, m).

bar_far._doc: Step 10 (the saloon as a room, #1157): the bar's north end, the loudmouth's; `bar_near` its south end, the undertaker's one drink.

room_talk_a._doc: Step 10: the room's second group (the brief's second table: standing talkers till sat talk is built), at the yard's back east of the way through, clear of the card table's chairs and the stranger's way round it.

room_bar_end._doc: Step 10: the saloon woman by the bar's north end, late.

stage_fiddle._doc: #938: Payday Night on saloon B's stage, the fiddler at its use point (#902), a hand off it clear of the stage's upright (a man's way to it is swept 0.3 m wide: at the point itself the upright's corner is 0.26 m off); the pianist at the stage's own upright.

book._doc: The book (townsfolk brief §3 "Three ways of being present"): a man indoors or asleep behind a front is a row here, not a body: no cost. A day's block with `in` (a place: a building's door, its lot id, or a way out of town such as `back@0`) puts him on it, doing `do`; he goes in and comes out at that place's door, never while you can see the last step (`seen_m`: past this far off nothing's seen). `doings`: what each shows from the street: `lamp` a lit window while it's `dark` [from, to] by the clock, `smoke` chimney smoke. A building shows them only while someone's in it doing one (BookLights; only buildings, not ways out).

calendar._doc: The town's day kinds (townsfolk brief §3 "The data"): a person's `day` is a list of blocks (every kind) or one list a kind (`ordinary` the default for any kind he hasn't). The town's day runs from `starts_h` to the next (a night's blocks past midnight belong to the day before). Each kind: `week_day` (the town's day number mod 7; day 1 a Monday) or `every` days from `first`, and an optional `if` (StoryState facts, as `talk`'s), the first that holds wins. PROPOSED: Sunday and a fortnight's payday on the Saturday; the story's kinds (mourning, uneasy) go here as `if` entries when the funeral and the news are built. `uneasy` (#1051, PROPOSED): the day after a killing or a shooting the town holds (TownNews sets StoryState news.yesterday at the day's turn; a story act's isn't counted, its day is the story's): the storekeeper keeps in, the loudmouth's out on the walk telling it.

people.name: Miner

people.name: Rancher

people.name: Fiddler

people.name: Piano player
people._doc: PROPOSED (#799, #938): the band's piano player, sat at the set's piano; Payday Night at the stage's upright; a stand-in body.

people.name: Doctor
people._doc: Townsfolk step 3 (#936), roster 2: the doctor's day self, the coroner. One man (#1095: there was an act-only `doc` too): the acts (SheriffDies, No Justice's office, the funeral) take him off his day (ValleyFolk.seize) and give him back; out on his walk in the afternoon only (the brief puts his crossing in 7-12; it waits for the act's morning to be free of him). He answers his door to any hurt man brought him (FetchHelp.at_door).

people.name: Storekeeper
people._doc: Roster 3: the general store's keeper; sweeps his walk at six, locks up at half past five, a drink in the saloon's second table till half nine (on the book: the saloon's room is step 10's). His own face (storekeeper_s1); the townsman's is a copy of it.

people.name: Storekeeper's wife
people._doc: Roster 4: the store, then its bench. A stand-in: the widow's model re-dressed (#851 pick 1: free copies; the sheriff's wife, an act man, wears the same body), seen at the bench only for two hours a day.

people.name: Livery man
people._doc: Roster 5: first up in the street, the last lamp but the saloon's; a drink in the saloon's second table 7-10. A stand-in: the rider model (the Baron's foreman wears it at the funeral). Door: the `livery` place (this file's `places`), its lot having no walk.

people.name: Blacksmith
people._doc: Roster 6: at the smithy's door from the first grey, west end. His own face (blacksmith_s1; Cody's stand-in wears it in a grey-blue shirt).

people.name: Hotel's landlady
people._doc: Roster 8: shakes a rug off the porch rail at six; on the porch for an hour at dusk. A stand-in: the widow's model re-dressed, as the store's wife (same body: kept apart, one at each end of the street).

people.name: Preacher
people._doc: Roster 9: the church is off the ground (up Church Lane, past the North-South Street's end): he walks down Main Street once, 8-9, and back. His own id because `preacher` is the funeral's act man (no hours): he's off the street before its ten o'clock. A stand-in: the undertaker's model in black.

people.name: Saloon woman
people._doc: Roster 16: asleep over the saloon till noon, on its porch for the lamps' hour, then in the room (on the book: the saloon's room is step 10's, and the yard's is No Law's). Her own face (working_girl_s3).

people.name: Cody
people._doc: Cody, who kills Earl (No Law beat 3, #773): one of the Baron's hired guns, a rough man. Not the red shirt (Sean on #796, 2026-11-11: the red shirt (Kett) is another man and isn't in the saloon; the stranger shot the sheriff, #905), so no red shirt on him. No hours: built with the rest and kept out till the act (NoLawMurder) takes him. A stand-in: the blacksmith's model (grey-blue work shirt) till the characters lane makes Cody.

people.name: Stranger
people._doc: The stranger who sits in the free chair and tells you not to move (No Law beat 3, #773). A stand-in man.

people.name: Townsman
people._doc: By day on the hotel's walk (No Law's scripts, docs/scripts/no_law.json: the townsman). Tells you the town's news: the sheriff shot (once he's brought in), and the morning after, Earl's murder as the town has it, or that you were sat at the table.

people.name: Loudmouth
people._doc: By day on the saloon's walk (the scripts' loudmouth): last night's bravado gone sour the morning after.

people.name: Undertaker
people._doc: On his walk by day. The morning after, Earl's laid out with him (ValleyFolk's morning: the body taken from the yard, a recorded death).

people.name: Townsman
people._doc: The young man the doctor sends to find you on day 2 (SheriffDies: "Harlan! Doc's asking for you.").

people.name: Sheriff
people._doc: The sheriff on the doctor's cot, day 2 (SheriffDies): the road's man (the_sheriff.json's model), built with the folk (a Studio man built in play is a long frame).

people.name: Mrs.
people._doc: The sheriff's wife at his bedside, day 2. A stand-in: the widow's model (the characters lane's), only used here; at the funeral (Funeral, #868) she's the widow.

people.name: Preacher
people._doc: The preacher at the grave (Funeral, #868). A stand-in: the undertaker's model in black (Sean's pick 1 on #851: the faceless folk are re-dressed copies).

people.name: The Baron
people._doc: The Baron, first seen at the sheriff's funeral (Funeral, #868): his offer to the widow. A stand-in till the characters lane makes him: the coat-and-cravat cowboy.

people.name: Foreman
people._doc: The Baron's foreman, a step behind him at the funeral, saying nothing (script setup S39). A stand-in man.

people.name: Cowboy
people._doc: The bold cowboy in the doctor's front office (No Justice step 2, NoJusticeCamp; his part is OPEN, s4: the card's one line). The bold cowboy's own model; No Law's stranger is a stand-in in it too.

_no_knock: #1095: places with no door to bang on (PlayerKnock): the saloon's set is its open yard. Elsewhere E at a door bangs on it only from outside it (ValleyFolk.past_door).
_doctor_room: #1095: where the doctor has a hurt man laid in his front room when he answers his door to him (FetchHelp.at_door, ValleyFolk.take_in): the doctor's building's own space [x, floor y, z] (config/moments/no_law_carry.json's laid spot, a step back).

dead._doc: The dead taken away (#1051; ValleyFolk._dead_step): a townsman killed in town and seen down (anyone holds it in TownNews), the undertaker comes for him within `seen_h` clock hours; unseen, from `morning_h` the next morning. He walks out to him (at most `walk_at_most_s`), and the body goes once you're `unseen_m` off it or it's out of your view. No Law's Earl keeps his own (`morning`).

regard._doc: How the town treats Harlan (townsfolk step 9, #1152; TownRegard; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5): each man's trust, fear, liking, respect (DESIGN §9) from 0, nudged by his own news (`view`: his TownNews view of Harlan; `fear_each_more` for each further man he has Harlan shooting) and the story's facts (`facts`: `if` StoryState as `talk`'s, `all` everyone, `who` one man's, `split` the town halves by each man's seed). Band: fear at `afraid_at` afraid; else trust, liking, respect averaged: `warm_at` warm, `cold_at` cold, between wary. What he shows within `show_m` (looked every `look_s`), again once you're `show_clear_m` further off. PROPOSED numbers, to be felt in play.

facts._doc: the sheriff brought in well: curious about the man from up the creek; the doctor's respect
he rode by the sheriff: wary to cold
No Law: he sat at the table and never moved (the town split, morning.you_were_there)
stood at the grave: the widow's word carries
No Justice, arrest: the first thing the law's done since the sheriff

Kett killed in the fight: plain respect and some fear

barks._doc: The barks (townsfolk step 9, TownBarks): the town's script's lines with an `if` (config/town_script.json), the most specific that fits; once a day a person, no line another said within `same_line_s`, one bark at you a group (`group_m`) as you pass (again once you're `group_clear_m` off it). `pools`: each man's pools in the script, his own first (`_default` the rest).

room._doc: The saloon at night as a room (townsfolk step 10, #1157; SaloonRoom, src/people/saloon_room.gd; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §6). Built on No Law's yard set (`set`: the bar, the card table, the piano), which is where the night's people are till the set moves into saloon B; `rect` [a0, b0, a1, b1] is the room on the set's lot (move the set and this with it). **Mood** 0 hushed to 1 roaring, once `every_s`: `people` x (how many are in of `full`) + `drink` x (their drink, 0-1: `drink_per_h` an hour at a drinking spot, `drinks` the doings that count) + `music` while the band sounds + the night's `add` (`nights`: the first whose `if` the story holds, else the day kind's in `kinds`) + Harlan's (`regard`: the town's band of him, only while he's in the room), times how many of the room are calm, times the climb back after trouble (nothing for `hold_s`, then up over `recover_s`). Names: under `hushed_under` hushed; under `calm_at` with trouble not yet lived down or Harlan in and the town cold or afraid: tense; under `lively_at` calm; else lively. **The director** (once `every_s`, only with you within `live_m`): a bit every `gap` seconds by the mood ([mood, least, most] rows, between them by the mood; none under `none_under`), picked by `weight` among `bits` whose `from` (his block's `do`, or `seated`) fits a calm man in the room at his chore who may speak; the same bit from the same man not within `again_s`. laugh: his table (`table_m`) grins, one laughs `second_s` late. toast: glass up and a `room.toast` line (the town's script), the bar lifts theirs. The events: a man coming in is hailed (`room.hail`) and lifts a hand; a man going says `room.leave` and one answers (`room.answer`); you coming in (not again within `enter_again_s`): the town warm, a hail from a warm man who sees you; cold or afraid, the talk drops (`drop`: the mood times `to`, easing back over `s`; mouths shut `quiet_s`; the `looks` nearest look round at you); the barkeep, warm, sets a glass down before you unasked once a night when you've stood `glass.wait_s` within `glass.m` of him (`room.glass`). **The hush** (`trouble`): a deed of `deeds` or a shot within `margin_m` of the room: each man who hasn't sensed it himself (Reaction) looks round `look` = base + per_m x his distance + nerve x his nerve seconds after (0.15 to 1.2), a man with `ducks` (the piano player) ducks instead. `sounds`: stand-ins (SynthSounds) till #807's takes: each one placed at its man. PROPOSED numbers, to be felt in play.
room._lights: The building whose window is lit (BookLights) while the room's open after dark with someone in: the saloon's, the yard set standing in for its room.

nights._doc: Night 2 (Sean's pick 4 C, #851): the night the sheriff dies the saloon is louder than ever.
The rest of the murder's night: what's left of the room is subdued.
Night 1, No Law: an ordinary night, a little bold (no sheriff tonight).

talk._doc: What the day folk say when you pass (`says` names a set here): within `near_m` of you, one line each `gap_s` at most, the first entry whose `if` the story holds (StoryState facts: a value, a list of values, "*" set at all, a key with ! not set), its words in turn. Each entry's id is its line in the scripts (docs/scripts/no_law.json, on PR #837's branch till it merges).

townsman._doc: PROPOSED (#868): the funeral's told by the town, not a marker; not in the scripts yet. The hour is config/moments/funeral.json's.

Sheriff's burying is this morning. Ten o'clock, up on the hill. Most of the town's going.

townsman._doc: PROPOSED (#868): said once if you watched from off; no more is made of it.

words: Sheriff's gone, then. And Doc's pinned his star on you. Well. Somebody had to.
Deputy, is it? You'll want to keep out of Cody's way.

townsman._doc: #1057: in place of morning.you_were_there when you carried Earl (No Law's script, #1056).
words: They say you carried him clear up the street. ... That his blood on you?
You were sat right there at the table, they say. And you never moved.
Cody shot Earl dead over the cards. Said there's no law left to save him. Bold as brass.
Earl drew first, I heard. Or reached, anyhow.
Three shots, they say. Or two. Nobody counted.
Sheriff's shot, they say. Laid up at the doc's.

undertaker._doc: PROPOSED (#796): not in the scripts yet.
words: Two in two days. The sheriff gets the good box; the county's paying for that one.
Earl. Shot through the head, before witnesses, by the man Cody. Pine box. Nobody's paying for a stone.

morning._doc: No Law's morning after (#796): once the murder's done (nolaw.murder done) and the clock's in `hours` (it can only get there through the night), nolaw.morning is set. Earl's body, if he's dead, is taken to the undertaker's once you're `unseen_m` off it or it's out of your view: gone from the yard for good, StoryState nolaw.earl = undertaker and death.earl his record. From `sheriff_from` (the clock) the dying sheriff's scene (SheriffDies, config/moments/sheriff_dies.json) starts, once.
morning.earl_death_doctor: Earl, the card player. Shot by Cody at the saloon's card table, the night after the sheriff was shot; a yard full of witnesses, and nobody stopped him. Dead on the way to the doctor's; laid out in his front room overnight, then at the undertaker's.
morning.earl_death: Earl, the card player. Shot through the head by Cody at the saloon's card table, the night after the sheriff was shot; a yard full of witnesses, and nobody stopped him. Laid out at the undertaker's.
